To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
intracellular creatine does not influence the response of the intact beating heart to acute oxidative stress.
creatine levels do NOT influence the response to ROS challenge in the heart.
Intracellular creatine content does not influence the response of the intact beating heart to acute oxidative stress.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular mechanisms that regulate the expression of the creatine transporters (CRTs), which are the only means by which creatine can be transported into cells.
the effects of oxidative stress in the heart.
the role of creatine in the pathophysiology of heart failure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
creatine is not a relevant antioxidant in the intact heart.
creatine does not protect against oxidative stress in the intact heart.
creatine is not a significant anti-oxidant for the intact beating heart.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
creatine supplementation is not cardioprotective in ischaemia-reperfusion injury.
the cardioprotectiveness of creatine in the heart is independent of its role as an antioxidant.
the heart is well protected from oxidative stress by other anti-oxidant systems, and that creatine supplementation is unlikely to be of benefit in cardiac diseases involving oxidative stress.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cardioprotectivity of creatine supplementation is likely mediated through other mechanisms.
the cardioprotected phenotype of CrT-OE hearts is unlikely due to enhanced antioxidant capacity, and that creatine deficiency alone is unlikely to be the cause of the cardiomyopathy in GAMT KO mice.
the functional deterioration of the isolated perfused heart is a very sensitive marker for oxidative stress and can be used to screen for novel anti-oxidant therapies.
